exposure: Use of NeuroMotion smartphone application for remote General Movements Assessment
outcome: Feasibility of the NeuroMotion smartphone application
Presence of fidgety movements (assessed by Prechtl's General Movements Assessment)
cohort: Thirty-one term-born infants at risk of cerebral palsy due to birth asphyxia or neonatal seizures, recruited from Paropakar Maternity and Women's Hospital in Kathmandu, Nepal.
finding: Engaging parents in screening for cerebral palsy using a smartphone-aided remote General Movements Assessment is feasible in an urban area of a South Asian lower middle-income country.
